title: Client-priority lease resume and ack timing adjustments (OpenAI compatibility)
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Several customer incidents exposed two related failure modes for long-lived streaming sessions behind the OpenAI-compatibility adapter: (1) aggressive server lease reclamation causing clients to observe abrupt cancels during short network blips, and (2) racey cancel acknowledgements that could lead to duplicate tool invocations when clients retried after a perceived cancel. This PR introduces a client-priority lease handoff and small adjustments to ack timing to reduce both user-visible cancels and duplicate tool calls while preserving server-side capacity efficiency.

Summary of changes: implement a lightweight persistent-lease state in the stream broker that marks certain sessions as "client-priority" for a configurable grace window (defaults: 10s soft-lease extension, 45s max suspend), add explicit cancel-ack handshake semantics to the OpenAI adapter so client soft-cancels are acknowledged and idempotency tokens exchanged, and introduce conservative server idle-timeout backoffs for sessions that previously hit premature eviction. This includes API-level compatibility behavior for the OpenAI adapter: unchanged public endpoints but different reconnect/resume behavior under the hood so downstream SDKs see fewer unexpected stream terminations.

Key behavioral rules (design notes): 1) Soft-cancel from client triggers a CANCEL-REQ frame; server returns CANCEL-ACK with a short-lived idempotency token. The token is required for toolcall replay after resume. 2) Disconnects with TCP/TLS loss enter a "snooze" state: server keeps session lease for soft_lease_seconds (default 10s) and extends up to suspend_max_seconds (default 45s) if client reconnects promptly and presents last-seen sequence. 3) For sessions flagged as client-priority (per route config or token), the broker delays lease reclamation by an additional jittered grace interval to avoid thundering herd evictions. 4) Server idle-timeouts are backoff-adjusted for sessions that previously produced many quick reconnects to avoid oscillation while not starving capacity.

Backward compatibility and rollout: All changes are designed to be opt-in via the route config flag stream.client_priority=true and a feature gate openai_adapter.soft_cancel_ack=true. By default we enable the soft-cancel ack path for beta customers only. Migration plan: start with Canary region + 5 internal teams, monitor reconnect rates and duplicate-toolcall counts for 72h, then enable globally in staged fashion.

Testing & verification: added unit tests around the cancel-ack state machine, integration tests that simulate intermittent network losses and assert no duplicate tool runs, and e2e smoke tests against the OpenAI-compat adapter. Load tests were run in the perf-lab to measure cost impact — median per-token latency increased by 0.6ms under heavy churn but duplicate-toolcall rate dropped from 0.84% to 0.02% in our simulated scenarios.

Notes for SDKs: The OpenAI-compat adapter now emits a "cancel_ack" event on the streaming SSE/WS path. SDK maintainers should treat this as a hint of idempotency token availability; SDKs that replay toolcalls must include the token to avoid server-side rejection. We included a short README in docs/api/reconnect.md describing how clients should attach tokens on resubmitted tool call payloads.

Rollout monitoring & alerts: new metrics: stream.suspend.count, stream.duplicate_toolcall.rate, stream.cancel_ack.latency. Added dashboards to Redwood Console and created an alert (P90 duplicate_toolcall.rate > 0.5% over 15m) to rollback if regression occurs.

Checklist: - [x] design doc and tabletop reviewed with SRE/security - [x] implementation + unit tests - [x] integration tests in CI - [x] perf lab verification - [x] docs updated (docs/api/reconnect.md) - [x] staged rollout configured

References: Linear ENG-2049 (stream stability), ENG-2072 (openai-compat reliability), support ticket SUP-4218 (customer incident).

Default behavior unchanged; enable via route config or the OpenAI adapter feature gate. Monitoring and rollback triggers added.
